correctness.rationale: For every finite rooted tree, infection indicators are products over unique root paths. A single path uses independent parental Q values, giving E I_u=q^{d(u)}. Pair paths for incomparable u,w share precisely a single duplicated parent variable at their LCA; joint probability is E Q² times q to the number of other distinct edges, while comparable pairs match percolation exactly. Variance expansion gives 2v times the nonnegative LCA-weighted pair polynomial. The combinatorial star upper bound and terminal broom lower bound and equality conditions are valid for every n>=3 and q in (0,1); v=0 is treated separately. Rational standalone checks exhaust all increasing-parent encodings through seven vertices and verify the Poisson contact exponential recovery formula. These finite checks are only supplementary.

originality.rationale: The closest 2026 source proves equality of tree infection marginals and notes outgoing edge correlations, while its simulation section treats variance of large random-network component sizes. Kenah and Robins (2007) establish exact epidemic percolation but not the finite-tree explicit shape optimum. Ramírez-Ramírez and Thompson (2013/2014) derive mean/variance formulas using random-network degree-law branching approximations and second transmissibility moments but do not encode arbitrary fixed rooted tree LCA positions. The new content is the exact polynomial of incomparable vertex pairs and a complete sharp extremal classification at each finite order, with an exact continuous-time example. Multiple semantic literature searches did not surface a matching same-claim item; this does not prove literature completeness.
residual_risks: An unindexed fixed-tree epidemic second-moment theorem might subsume the polynomial or extremizers; semantic search nonappearance is not proof of absence.

The general exact epidemic-percolation representation in Kenah--Robins theoretically permits deriving any finite-tree moment, so the originality claim is restricted to the explicit closed coefficient and shape extremizers, not computability of outbreak variance.

value.rationale: For a known finite contact tree, matched independent bond percolation predicts identical expected epidemic burden while potentially underestimating its variance. The closed pair/branch polynomial separates marginal transmissibility variability from the known rooted contact structure. Sharp extrema distinguish zero error (seeded chain), the smallest nonzero error (single distal split), and the maximal error (rooted star), providing quantitative variability diagnostics and precise network-placement limits. This is not a claim that generic variance effects are new.
